claim: Every scene load zeroes exactly flags $0000-$000F (STX $eventFlags with X = $0000, 16-bit) and leaves $0A02 and up untouched; the call site is ExecuteSceneTransition only.

trial.control: write $FF to $0A02 and $0A03, take a scene exit, read $0A00-$0A03 after the new scene is running
trial.forced: write $FF to $0A00 and $0A01 first, take the same exit
observe: break on write to $0A00 with the PC at 253291 (ClearSceneState)

confirms: $0A00 and $0A01 read $00 (except bits the new scene sets) and $0A02/$0A03 keep $FF
refutes: any other bit of $0A00-$0A01 survives, or $0A02 changes

claim: The inventory overlay pushes the flags word $0A00, zeroes it (the overlay exit flag is flag $0000), clears flag $FF, and on close restores the word and sets flag $FF again.

trial.control: open the inventory without touching the flags
trial.forced: write $A5 to $0A00 and $5A to $0A01, open and close the inventory
observe: $0A00-$0A01 while the overlay is open (expect 0 until the menu sets bit 0)

confirms: values zero during the overlay and return unchanged
refutes: values leak into the overlay or are not restored

claim: The kill-flag block is zeroed only by world-map entry (WorldMapController), st68_kara, sp58_red_eye and a real game over; ordinary scene changes, a revive, a save and a load keep it.

trial.control: write $FF to $0A80-$0A9F, take an ordinary scene exit, read the block
trial.forced: same start, then (a) enter the world map, (b) die with 100 gems or more (revive), (c) die with fewer than 100 gems (real game over), (d) save and load
observe: execution of ClearAllWramFlags (46284) and of the loop at 54988

confirms: block unchanged after the control, (b) and (d); zero after (a) and (c)
refutes: any other reset point, or a reset at the control

claim: Spine flag $00FF is the scene-setup-complete latch: cleared at the top of ClearSceneState and at overlay open, set after setup; thinkers that set it and park on a clear wait resume only when the next clear happens.

trial.control: watch bit 7 of $0A1F across a scene load
trial.forced: open and close the inventory in scene $01 (flag_gated_palette_warm active) and in scene $0A (alarm palette)
observe: whether the palette bundle replays after close

confirms: latch pattern clear, set; palette replays after close in the thinker scenes
refutes: no replay (the thinker does not resume) or a clear from another writer

claim: In scene $3F byte $0A01 is the laborer counter: each hit on a dm3F_switch increments it, dm3F_mine_collapse_trigger fires at exactly 4.

trial.forced: hit the four switches, then watch flag $0121 and the BG change

confirms: counter reaches 4 and the cave-in runs
refutes: a D1 flag in $08-$0F set by another actor in scene $3F changes the count

claim: Rama gives the Mystic Statue only when the low byte of $0A00 equals $FE (flags $0001-$0007 set, flag $0000 clear), checked by LDA $eventFlags; AND #$00FF; CMP #$00FE.

trial.control: set $0A00 = $7E (flag $0007 missing) and talk to Rama
trial.forced: set $0A00 = $FE and talk to Rama; repeat with $FF

confirms: only $FE gives the statue dialog and sets flag $000F

claim: The plate gate opener fires when bits 1-4 of $0A00 (flags $0001-$0004, one per gold tile) are all set (AND #$001E equals $001E).
The tomb Dark Space portal (gw88_tomb_dark_space) appears when byte $0A9F equals $3F: kill flags $04F8-$04FD (the six stone archers) set and $04FE/$04FF clear.

trial.control: kill five of the six stone archers

refutes: portal after five, or $0A9F has other bits set in normal play

claim: Scene-meta gate: scene $06 loads the main-character sprite set (meta_label_23) when flag $21 is set and $4C is clear.

trial.control: warp to scene $06 with $21 and $4C clear
trial.forced: warp with $21 set; then with $4C set (and $21 clear); then both set
observe: sprite set loaded (spm_sc06_castle_actors, spm_sc02_main_characters or the South Cape set)

confirms: $21 alone selects the main characters, $4C wins over $21

claim: Scene-meta gate: scene $06 loads the shared South Cape interior art (meta_label_01) when flag $4C is set; meaning of the flag in story terms is not established.
confirms: interior art and sprites change with $4C

claim: Scene-meta gate: scenes $5A and $5C skip the prison-enemy sprites and load the Freejia sprite set (meta_label_0C of scene $32) when flag $70 is set.

observe: sprite VRAM and OAM (prison enemies versus Freejia sprites)

confirms: sprite set switches; enemies placed in the scene render with the other set

claim: Scene-meta gates: flag $7B loads the half-drained Mu effect tilemap in scenes $5F, $60, $61, $62; set by the west pedestal of the Statue of Hope.

trial.forced: warp with $7B set; then with $7E set; then both

confirms: half effect for $7B, drained for $7E, drained when both

claim: Scene-meta gates: flag $7E loads the drained Mu effect tilemap in scenes $5F, $60, $61, $62, $64, $65; set by the east pedestal of the Statue of Hope.
confirms: drained tilemap in all six scenes
refutes: a scene keeps the undrained tilemap

claim: Scene-meta gate: scene $67 loads the Nazca sprite set (meta_label_22 of scene $49) instead of the vampire sprites when flag $88 is set.

observe: sprite VRAM, vampire actors (they use the vampire sprites)

claim: Scene-meta gate: scene $78 loads pal_watermia_dark when flag $96 is set (pal_watermia otherwise).
Scene-meta gate: scene $AC plays bgm_blessing_of_nature when flag $B3 is set, bgm_ominous_whispers otherwise.
Scene-meta gate: scene $8C loads map_prologue_prophecy_2 when flag $F4 is set, map_prologue_prophecy otherwise.
Bytes with no static site ('unassigned') are never written during a normal playthrough.

trial.control: a write watch on $0A02-$0AB3 that logs PC and value, with a positive control (write to $0A02 by a script)
trial.forced: play through the early game and a full dungeon, open menus, die, save, load
observe: bytes written by an indirect or dynamic path

confirms: no write to the listed bytes
refutes: a write names its code path and may reveal an unlisted owner

claim: The new-game path (DiaryNewGameStart, 779502-779557) writes no byte of the flag array, so a new game starts with whatever the array holds; after boot that is all zero.

trial.control: cold boot, choose new game, read $0A00-$0AB3 (expect all zero)
trial.forced: load a save with many flags set, return to the title screen by any available path (soft reset or menu), choose new game, read the array
observe: whether any path returns to the title without the boot clear

confirms: array zero after new game, or no path back to the title without the clear
refutes: stale flags survive a new game
